Apple___Apple_scab.Environment: Cool, wet and humid conditions, especially during spring.
Apple___Apple_scab.Spread: Rain splash, airborne spores and infected fallen leaves.
Apple___Apple_scab.Description: Apple Scab is a fungal disease that affects apple leaves and fruits. It produces olive-green to dark lesions and can reduce fruit quality and yield.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small olive-green spots appear on young leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions become darker and spread across leaves and fruits.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves may curl and fall, while fruits develop dark scabby lesions.

Recommended_Actions: Begin treatment early in the season.

Apple___Black_rot.Environment: Warm and humid conditions with prolonged moisture.
Apple___Black_rot.Spread: Rain splash, infected branches, dead wood and mummified fruits.
Apple___Black_rot.Description: Black Rot is a fungal disease that causes leaf spots, cankers on branches and dark rotting lesions on apple fruits.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small purple or brown spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaf lesions enlarge and branch cankers develop.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Fruits develop black rot and may become completely mummified.

Prevention: Prune trees to improve air circulation.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Environment: Warm and humid conditions with spring rainfall.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Spread: Wind-borne fungal spores between apple and cedar/juniper hosts.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Description: Cedar Apple Rust is a fungal disease that produces bright yellow-orange spots on apple leaves and can affect developing fruits.
Cause: Presence of cedar or juniper host plants

Age_Cycle.Early: Small yellow-orange spots appear on the upper surface of leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots enlarge and orange structures develop on the underside of leaves.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Severely infected leaves may drop early and fruit development can be affected.

Organic_Treatment: Remove nearby infected host material where practical
Prevention: Monitor plants during wet spring weather.
Manage nearby cedar or juniper hosts where appropriate.
Recommended_Actions: Begin treatment when symptoms first appear.

Apple___healthy.Environment: Adequate sunlight, balanced nutrition, suitable temperature and well-drained soil.
Apple___healthy.Description: The apple plant appears healthy with normal green foliage, healthy growth and no visible signs of disease or pest damage.
Prevention: Prune appropriately for good air circulation.
Recommended_Actions: Monitor regularly for early disease symptoms.

Blueberry___healthy.Environment: Cool to moderate temperatures, acidic well-drained soil, adequate sunlight and sufficient moisture.
Blueberry___healthy.Description: The blueberry plant appears healthy with vigorous growth, green foliage and normal fruit development without visible disease symptoms.
Recommended_Actions: Inspect plants regularly for early disease symptoms.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Environment: Warm and humid conditions with poor air circulation.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Spread: Wind-borne fungal spores and infected plant material.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Description: Powdery Mildew is a fungal disease that produces a white powdery growth on cherry leaves and shoots. Severe infections can reduce photosynthesis and fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small white powdery patches appear on young leaves and shoots.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: The white fungal growth spreads across leaves and shoots.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves become distorted and plant growth and fruit development may be reduced.

Recommended_Actions: Begin treatment at the first signs of infection.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Environment: Suitable temperature, adequate sunlight, balanced nutrition and well-drained soil.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Description: The cherry plant appears healthy with normal green foliage, vigorous growth, flowering and fruit development without visible disease symptoms.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Disease: Cercospora Leaf Spot / Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Spread: Wind, rain splash and infected crop residue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Description: Gray Leaf Spot is a fungal disease of corn that produces elongated gray to brown lesions on leaves and can significantly reduce photosynthesis and yield.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small tan to gray spots appear on lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions become elongated and spread across leaves.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large portions of leaves become necrotic and dry, reducing yield.

Recommended_Actions: Apply fungicide when disease pressure is high.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Environment: Cool to moderate temperatures with high humidity and frequent moisture.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Description: Common Rust is a fungal disease that produces reddish-brown to orange rust-colored pustules on corn leaves.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small pale spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Rust-colored pustules develop on both leaf surfaces.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Heavy infection causes premature leaf drying and reduced photosynthesis.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Environment: Cool to moderate temperatures with high humidity and prolonged leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Spread: Wind, rain splash and infected crop residue.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Description: Northern Leaf Blight is a fungal disease characterized by large elongated gray-green to brown lesions on corn leaves.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small gray-green lesions appear on lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge into long cigar-shaped areas.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large portions of foliage become necrotic, reducing photosynthesis and grain filling.

Prevention: Remove or properly manage infected residue.
Monitor crops during cool wet periods.
Recommended_Actions: Apply treatment when disease pressure increases.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.Environment: Adequate sunlight, suitable temperature, balanced nutrition and sufficient soil moisture.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Description: The corn plant appears healthy with vigorous growth, green leaves and normal development without visible disease symptoms.
Recommended_Actions: Inspect plants regularly for early disease symptoms.

Grape___Black_rot.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Grape___Black_rot.Spread: Rain splash, wind, infected berries and crop debris.
Grape___Black_rot.Description: Grape Black Rot is a fungal disease that affects leaves, shoots and berries. It can cause dark lesions and severe fruit rot, resulting in significant crop losses.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small tan or reddish-brown spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge and dark fruit spots develop.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Berries become dark, shriveled and mummified.

Treatment: Remove infected berries and plant material.
Prune vines to improve air circulation.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Environment: Warm growing conditions combined with vine stress and infected pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Spread: Infected planting material, pruning wounds, fungal spores and contaminated tools.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Description: Esca is a complex grapevine trunk disease that affects the woody tissues of vines and may cause characteristic leaf symptoms, berry discoloration and gradual vine decline.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small interveinal yellow or reddish areas appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaf symptoms become more pronounced and vines show reduced vigor.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves may dry rapidly, berries can develop dark spots and vines may decline or die.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease development can occur over multiple growing seasons.

Treatment: Replace severely affected vines when necessary.
Recommended_Chemicals: No reliable curative chemical treatment is available for established trunk infection.
Recommended_Actions: Replace severely affected vines when required.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Environment: Warm and humid conditions with prolonged leaf moisture.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Spread: Wind, rain splash and infected plant debris.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Description: Grape Leaf Blight, also known as Isariopsis Leaf Spot, produces dark lesions on grape leaves and can cause premature defoliation when infection is severe.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small reddish-brown or dark spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots enlarge and become more numerous.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large portions of leaves become necrotic and premature defoliation may occur.

Grape___healthy.Environment: Adequate sunlight, balanced nutrition, suitable temperature and well-drained soil.
Grape___healthy.Description: The grapevine appears healthy with green foliage, vigorous shoots and normal flowering and berry development without visible disease symptoms.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Environment: Warm subtropical and tropical conditions that support citrus psyllid populations.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Spread: Primarily transmitted by infected citrus psyllids and infected propagation material.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Description: Huanglongbing, commonly called Citrus Greening, is a serious citrus disease that causes leaf mottling, poor fruit development and gradual decline of affected trees.

Age_Cycle.Early: Leaves develop uneven yellow mottling and shoots may show reduced growth.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaves become increasingly mottled and fruits develop poorly.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Branches decline, fruits remain small and misshapen, and the tree may eventually die.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease progression can occur over months or several years.

Treatment: There is no reliable cure for an infected tree.
Remove severely infected trees where recommended.
Recommended_Chemicals: No curative chemical treatment is available for established infection.
Psyllid-control insecticides may be used according to local recommendations.
Prevention: Inspect new plants before introducing them into orchards.
Recommended_Actions: Remove severely infected trees according to local guidance.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.Environment: Warm, humid and rainy conditions with prolonged leaf wetness.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Spread: Rain splash, infected plant material and contaminated tools.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Description: Bacterial Spot is a bacterial disease that causes dark lesions on peach leaves and fruits. Severe infection can cause premature leaf drop and reduced fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots become dark and may develop yellow halos.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves drop prematurely and fruits develop dark sunken lesions.

Peach___healthy.Environment: Adequate sunlight, balanced nutrition, suitable temperature and well-drained soil.
Peach___healthy.Description: The peach tree appears healthy with normal green foliage, vigorous growth, flowering and fruit development without visible disease symptoms.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Spread: Rain splash, contaminated seeds, irrigation water and infected tools.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Description: Bacterial Spot affects pepper leaves and fruits, producing dark lesions that can reduce plant vigor and fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots become dark and enlarge, while fruit lesions may develop.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Severe leaf drop and fruit lesions can reduce crop yield and quality.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.Environment: Warm temperatures, adequate sunlight, balanced nutrition and well-drained soil.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Description: The bell pepper plant appears healthy with green foliage, vigorous growth and normal flowering and fruit development.

Potato___Early_blight.Environment: Warm temperatures with alternating wet and dry conditions and stressed plants.
Potato___Early_blight.Spread: Wind, rain splash, infected plant debris and infected tubers.
Potato___Early_blight.Description: Potato Early Blight is a fungal disease that produces characteristic dark lesions with concentric rings on potato leaves and stems.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small dark spots appear on older lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots enlarge and develop concentric target-like rings.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large areas of foliage become necrotic and leaves drop prematurely.

Potato___Late_blight.Environment: Cool, wet and humid conditions with prolonged leaf wetness.
Potato___Late_blight.Spread: Wind-borne spores, rain splash, infected plants and infected tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.Description: Potato Late Blight is a highly destructive disease that can rapidly damage foliage and tubers under cool and wet conditions.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked dark lesions appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge rapidly and white fungal growth may appear under humid conditions.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Entire foliage collapses and tubers may develop brown rot.

Recommended_Actions: Inspect fields frequently during wet weather.

Potato___healthy.Environment: Adequate sunlight, balanced nutrition, suitable temperature, proper irrigation and well-drained soil.
Potato___healthy.Description: The potato plant appears healthy with vigorous green foliage and normal tuber development without visible disease symptoms.

Raspberry___healthy.Environment: Cool to moderate temperatures, adequate sunlight, good drainage and balanced soil moisture.
Raspberry___healthy.Description: The raspberry plant appears healthy with vigorous growth, green foliage and normal flowering and fruit development without visible disease symptoms.

Soybean___healthy.Environment: Warm temperatures, adequate sunlight, fertile well-drained soil and balanced moisture.
Soybean___healthy.Description: The soybean plant appears healthy with vigorous growth, green foliage and normal pod development without visible disease symptoms.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.Environment: Warm temperatures, high humidity and poor air circulation.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Spread: Wind-borne fungal spores, infected plant debris and contaminated tools.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Description: Powdery Mildew is a common fungal disease of squash that produces a white powdery coating on leaves and stems. Severe infection can reduce photosynthesis and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small white powdery patches appear on older leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: White fungal growth spreads across leaves and stems.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves become yellow, dry and may die prematurely, reducing fruit development.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Spread: Rain splash, infected leaves and contaminated plant material.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Description: Strawberry Leaf Scorch is a fungal disease that causes numerous dark purple to reddish spots on strawberry leaves. Severe infection can reduce plant vigor and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small dark purple spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots enlarge and merge, causing larger areas of leaf damage.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large portions of leaves become necrotic and plant vigor decreases.

Strawberry___healthy.Environment: Moderate temperatures, adequate sunlight, good drainage and balanced moisture.
Strawberry___healthy.Description: The strawberry plant appears healthy with green foliage, normal flowering and healthy fruit development without visible disease symptoms.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Spread: Rain splash, contaminated seeds, irrigation water and infected plant material.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Description: Tomato Bacterial Spot causes small dark lesions on leaves, stems and fruits. Severe infection can cause defoliation and reduce fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots become dark and enlarge, sometimes developing yellow halos.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves may drop and fruits develop dark raised or scabby lesions.

Tomato___Early_blight.Environment: Warm temperatures, high humidity and prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Early_blight.Spread: Wind, rain splash, infected crop debris and contaminated tools.
Tomato___Early_blight.Description: Tomato Early Blight is a fungal disease characterized by dark lesions with concentric rings on leaves and stems. Severe infection can reduce plant vigor and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small dark spots appear on older lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge and develop characteristic concentric rings.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large areas of foliage become necrotic and leaves drop prematurely.

Treatment: Improve plant nutrition and field sanitation.

Tomato___Late_blight.Environment: Cool, wet and humid conditions with prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Late_blight.Spread: Wind, rain splash, infected plants and infected plant material.
Tomato___Late_blight.Description: Tomato Late Blight is a highly destructive disease that can rapidly damage leaves, stems and fruits under cool and wet conditions.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked dark lesions appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge rapidly and may develop white fungal growth under humid conditions.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large areas of foliage collapse and fruits develop brown lesions.

Prevention: Monitor crops during cool wet weather.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with poor air circulation and high relative humidity.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Spread: Airborne spores, rain splash and infected plant material.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Description: Tomato Leaf Mold is a fungal disease that primarily affects tomato leaves. Yellow patches appear on the upper leaf surface while olive-green to brown fungal growth develops underneath.

Age_Cycle.Early: Pale yellow spots appear on the upper surface of leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Olive-green or brown fungal growth develops on the underside.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves curl, dry and fall prematurely, reducing plant vigor.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Spread: Rain splash, wind, infected plant debris and contaminated tools.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Description: Septoria Leaf Spot is a fungal disease that produces numerous small circular spots with dark borders and pale centers on tomato leaves.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small circular spots appear on lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots enlarge and develop pale centers with dark margins.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves become heavily infected, yellow and fall prematurely.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Environment: Hot, dry conditions with low humidity and plant stress.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Spread: Wind, movement between plants, contaminated plant material and farm equipment.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny pests that feed on tomato leaves, causing stippling, yellowing and webbing. Heavy infestations can severely reduce plant vigor.

Age_Cycle.Early: Tiny pale spots or stippling appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaves become yellow or bronze and fine webbing may appear.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves dry and drop, and severe infestations can stunt or kill plants.

Treatment: Wash plants with suitable water spray where practical.
Prevention: Control weeds that may host mites.
Encourage beneficial insects and predatory mites.
Recommended_Actions: Inspect leaves for stippling and webbing.

Tomato___Target_Spot.Environment: Warm, humid conditions with prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Spread: Wind, rain splash and infected plant debris.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Description: Target Spot is a fungal disease that causes circular brown lesions with concentric rings on tomato leaves, stems and fruits.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small brown spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Spots enlarge and develop concentric rings.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large lesions develop on leaves and fruits, causing defoliation and fruit damage.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Environment: Warm conditions that favor whitefly populations.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Spread: Primarily transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly, Bemisia tabaci.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Description: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus causes severe leaf curling, yellowing and stunted growth. Infected plants may produce few or no marketable fruits.

Age_Cycle.Early: Young leaves begin curling upward and show yellowing.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Plant growth becomes stunted and leaves become increasingly curled.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Plants remain severely stunted and fruit production is greatly reduced.

Treatment: There is no curative treatment for infected plants.
Recommended_Chemicals: Insecticides for whitefly management according to local recommendations.
Prevention: Use insect-proof nursery structures where appropriate.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Environment: Virus can persist on contaminated surfaces, tools and plant material.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Spread: Mechanical contact, contaminated tools, hands, seeds and infected plant material.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Description: Tomato Mosaic Virus causes characteristic light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves and can lead to distorted growth and reduced fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Light and dark green mosaic patterns appear on young leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaves become distorted and plant growth slows.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Plants may become stunted and fruit development and quality may be reduced.

Symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern
Treatment: There is no curative treatment for infected plants.
Use virus-free seeds and planting material.
Recommended_Chemicals: No curative chemical treatment is available.
Prevention: Avoid handling healthy plants after infected plants.

Tomato___healthy.Environment: Adequate sunlight, suitable temperature, balanced nutrition and proper irrigation.
Tomato___healthy.Description: The tomato plant appears healthy with green foliage, vigorous growth and normal flowering and fruit development without visible disease or pest symptoms.
